items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: And one day, Miss Gracie told me, Harps is fee. You have an opportunity of learning things that you will never be able to pay for.

ctx.x: So you had to learn all of those languages too?

Well, you know, young, I was young and foolish at last. And one day, Miss Gracie told me, Harps is fee. You have an opportunity of learning things that you will never be able to pay for. And you're there giggling and giggling. And after a while, I said, well, I think Miss Gracie is right. Let me stop giggling and pay attention to what... What I...the opportunity that I had. So there's where I began to catch on. A little German. A little Spanish. Well, I knew French well.
When did you learn English? When did you learn English? Well, with everybody.

items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Grace King's mother. I worked there.

ctx.x: And was, Bill says, was French the only language you could read in?

Well, it's the language that I could read with more facilité, you know. Yes. But I read because, you see, old Mrs. W. W. King, Grace King. Her mother? Huh? Grace King's mother? Grace King's mother. I worked there. And there they used to have classes every three, about four days in the week. One day it would be Capitán de Chivarria, that was for the Spanish. And nothing but Spanish. And they speak it to me and I dig it like a little young crazy thing, you know. I wasn't twenty years old. Then one day it was Herman…
And which language did Guayari teach?
